[W1486656280] (2009, transport) Light-rail systems around the world. The main difference between light rail transit and heavy rail vehicle and classical urban railway systems is that light rail vehicles are able to share road surfaces with other road users. Light rail is characterized by low axle loads, the ability to negotiate tight curves, and the fact that vehicles are generally not driven faster than the driver's view of the line ahead permits for safe braking. This article provides an overview of light rail systems globally including their historical development, optimization efforts, planning parameters, and systems analysis.

Compared with other forms of urban rail transit,joint operation can improve the efficiency of transporting passengers.Based on an analysis of current joint operation both at home and abroad,and also on contrastive studies between domestic projects of urban rail network,the paper explores effective ways of combining joint operation and rail transit network with a view to offer some help to improve urban rail construction.

[W2390191936] (2013, transport) The optimization for rolling stock assignment of urban rail transit network. This paper presents an optimization approach for rolling stock assignment of urban rail transit network to response the new tendency of urban rail transit from single-rail to network operation.We further give the single-depot and multi-depot rolling stock assignment models.We solve the problem by ILOG CPLEX 12.5 and combination with a numeric example.It is proved to be effective by comparison with a heuristic algorithm.Result proves that the method can provide a good reference for rolling stock assignment in urban rail transit network.

[W650451976] (2003, transport) LIGHT RAIL VEHICLE DESIGNS LOOK TO THE FUTURE. This article presents some highlights of the design features of the new generation of Light Rail Vehicles. They trace their basic look back to the Eurotram vehicle that went into operation in Strasbourg, France, in 1994. The sloping cab front and platinum coloring set the new tone. Color schemes are important because of the push to attract and hold new riders. Low-floor designs make the vehicle more accessible and easier to maintain. They also increase capacity by eliminating dead space occupied by steps. Generally the plans call for a 70/30 split between low-floor and high-floor layouts. A new philosophy called universal design, which breaks away from the generic, aggregate proportions aimed at some average rider, incorporates elements that serve all sizes and types of riders.

[W562290735] (2008, transport) Pacific Transit Trifecta. This article describes three different approaches to the growth of rail transit in the Pacific Northwest. The transit programs are highlighted for their approach to rail transit as an economic development tool that is presented with an environmentally friendly approach. The rail transit systems profiled include: 1) Portland, Oregon and its MAX light rail line, the Portland Streetcar merging light rail with traditional streetcar, and the West Side Express commuter rail service; 2) Seattle, Washington and its Sound Transit light rail transit system; and, 3) the SkyTrain Advanced Light Rail Transit and the West Coast Express commuter service operated by Translink in Vancouver, British Columbia.

[W2528808465] (2016, transport) Revolutionising transport in the Holy City. Impressive ridership figures have been reported for Jerusalem's inaugural light rail line since its 2011 opening. The city's plans to further expand the light rail's reach are discussed in this article, based on conversations with the people involved with this sometimes controversial project. Fleet utilization, public support, as well as the design of new projects are among the issues presented here.

[W68226248] (2013, transport) The Exposition Light Rail Line Study: a Before and After Study of the Impact of New Light Rail Transit Service. A detailed study shows changes in travel behavior around new Exposition (Expo) Line light rail stations in Los Angeles. The Expo Line runs 8.7 miles from downtown Los Angeles. The six western-most stations along the Expo Line comprise the experimental neighborhoods, and similar control group neighborhoods were chosen nearby. This research project enrolled experimental households, within ½ mile of a new Expo Line station, and control households, living beyond ½ mile from the station. In fall of 2011, those households were asked to track their travel for seven days. In approximately half of the households, an adult also carried a GPS device and an accelerometer, to measure travel and physical activity. Evidence shows that the Expo Line is associated with large reductions in VMT, some increase in rail transit ridership, changes in physical activity, and large reductions in GHG emissions among households living within ½ mile of a station. The research design, using a control group to account for factors other than the rail investment, allows causal inferences to be made more strongly than is often the case in social scientific research. Viewed from the perspective of the greater Los Angeles region, these impacts will be small, but they are large in the neighborhoods surrounding the Expo Line.

[W2372201022] (2013, transport) Research on Intercity Rail Transit Network Planning Scheme for Wanjiang District in Anhui Province. At present,the development planning for Wanjiang urban agglomeration in Anhui Province has been raised to national strategy.Wanjiang district,which is a key development district for accelerating the national Rise of Central China Plan,is being in a rapid development stage,so it is necessary to formulate an intercity rail transit planning scheme for this urban agglomeration.In this paper,based on the characteristic of Wanjiang urban agglomeration,the principle and method for rail transit planning in accordance with the actual situation of Wanjiang district are put out.Furthermore,through analysis on space joint and traffic corridor of Wanjiang district,and through using representative 'point-line-plane' factor analytic method,the intercity rail transit network in Wanjiang district is divided into two subnets in which the one is a main backbone intercity sub-network and the other is an urban agglomeration intercity sub-network.It can serve as a more reasonable intercity rail transit network planning scheme for Wanjiang urban agglomeration.

[W2916187127] (2019, transport) Do light rail transit investments increase employment opportunities? The case of Charlotte, North Carolina. Abstract This paper examines whether rail transit stations tend to increase employment opportunities in nearby neighbourhoods and whether rail transit tends to be placed in neighbourhoods which connects to higher‐wage jobs. The results show no significant relative increase in the level of employment in neighbourhoods near rail stations post opening of the first light rail line in Charlotte, NC. However, the line connects to areas with significantly higher shares of high‐wage workers and industries. While creating accessibility to higher‐skilled jobs may result in greater economic impacts, it may conflict with goals of increasing employment opportunities for transit dependent, lower‐wage workers.
